title: Gesture-induced scroll & density inconsistencies audit for UI Kit across mobile Safari and Firefox Focus
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Scope: Investigate and triage a set of cross-browser, gesture- and density-related visual regressions observed in the UI Kit on mobile WebKit (Safari) and Firefox Focus. Focus areas: token-driven spacing/scale, button/touch-target misalignment, table header jitter on fast swipes, and pixel‑alignment artifacts in Canvas/SVG charts.

Goals:
- Produce reproducible steps for each issue and map them to likely root causes (CSS/paint, token mapping, runtime transforms).
- Categorize severity (blocking/degraded/minor) and propose concrete fixes for each class.
- Produce a short patch plan (design recommendation, engineering tasks, test matrix) and owners.

Acceptance criteria:
- Each issue has 1) repro steps, 2) suggested fix, 3) estimated engineering effort, 4) test case added to QA matrix (device+browser+orientation).
- Design provides updated token guidance for density/scaling and a fallback spec for WebKit quirks.
- One pilot PR merged fixing the highest-severity table-jitter case (or a mitigatory CSS workaround).
steps_to_reproduce: iPhone 14 / iOS 17.2 / Safari: Open dashboard > large data table, perform a fast upward swipe on rows 10–25 -> observe header translate/jitter and row misalignment.
iPhone 12 mini / iOS 16.8 / Safari: Toggle system text size to Large (accessibility) and visit Settings modal -> primary buttons show clipped touch area despite token scaling.
Pixel 6 / Android 13 / Firefox Focus: Navigate to Reports > Chart canvas, pinch zoom then swipe horizontally -> chart axes sometimes blur (subpixel rendering) and tooltips misposition.
iPad Air / iPadOS Safari: Two-finger drag on a table with sticky columns -> column outlines shift and drop shadows reflow, causing perceived visual jump.
Android Pixel / Chrome: With hw-acceleration disabled (simulated), tokens controlling elevation and transform produce different stacking than on Safari -> compare screenshots.
updates: 2025-02-18: Ticket created after QA flagged three anomalies in weekly cross-browser sweep. Initial triage suggests a mix of token scaling + WebKit-specific overscroll behavior.
2025-02-19: Design triage meeting — prioritized table header jitter as P1; Diego to capture high-fidelity repro GIFs and frame-by-frame scroll traces.

2025-02-20: Engineering note (ENG-5210) indicates sticky positioning + transform combos are expensive on WebKit and can cause layout thrashing. Suggested workaround: avoid translateY on sticky headers; use top with will-change: transform for limited scenarios.

2025-02-22: Design proposed token change: introduce 'density-tier' clamp function for spacing tokens and update token scaling rules for dynamic type. Shared Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/REDACTED/ui-kit-density-audit

2025-02-24: Created a small pilot PR to add '-webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch' and a constrained 'overscroll-behavior: contain' pair to the table container; PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui-kit/pull/879. Observed reduction in header bounce during fast swipes (QA: needs more device coverage).
2025-02-25: Design review scheduled with PM and Eng to finalize fallback token map and pick an engineering owner for chart pixel-alignment fixes (candidate: ENG-5101).
notes: Workaround-first approach: apply mitigations that reduce user impact while engineering investigates root causes requiring runtime/kernel changes.
Consider landing a small token shim in the runtime (server-side class) for Private deployments that disable aggressive transform optimizations as a temporary toggle for customers.
Cross-team ask: ask infra to provide a WebKit lab device for reproducible CI runs (pinpointing to exact webkit versions).
